payload: Every host serves one API at fnPath. A board's address is the first 24 hex chars of the sha-256 of its pairing code; possession of the id is read AND write (writes travel with the id as x-rc-key). The relay carries the extension's own board webview: the page is media/board.js verbatim behind a bridge, the extension pushes the frames it would post to that webview, and the page queues the messages that webview would post back. GET ?id=<boardId>[&since=<seq>][&wait=<secs>] returns { ok, seq, at, writes, mv, frame?, events[] } — frame (the latest { type:'state', state } with state.composer.models split out) only when it is newer than since, events (host-to-page messages: searchResults, mentions, voice, remote dialogs and toasts) newer than since, at most eventsMax retained; wait is honoured only by hosts that can hold a request. GET ?id=<boardId>&models=1 returns { ok, mv, models[] }; GET ?id=<boardId>&msgs=1 returns { ok, msgs[], viewerAt }. POST { kind:'frame', at, writes, mv, state?, models? } REPLACES the frame (state absent = heartbeat, at only) and answers { ok, mv, viewerAt, msgs[] }; POST { kind:'event', events[] } appends host-to-page events; POST { kind:'msg', nonce, msg:{ type, ... } } queues one webview message for the pushing machine — msg.type matches typeOk, the JSON is at most msgMaxBytes, at most msgMax queued — and whether it runs is the extension's decision (remote.writes), never the relay's; POST { kind:'ack', nonces[] } removes acked messages (at-least-once). The static page and all three hosts (Netlify functions, Cloudflare Worker, plain Node) speak exactly this.
